_doc: What the ground is made of: twenty materials, each with its colours, its relief (a normal map) and its heights, packed by tools/ground/build.py (the Ground workflow) into two atlases of 5 x 4 cells. Nineteen are scans from the free libraries (public domain, CC0: polyhaven.com, ambientcg.com), most of them taken from the air, so that they hold up when the game lays them out large; the canopy of a wood is made by the packer itself (no library has one). The game lays every material at a ladder of sizes, from twelve metres a repeat to two hundred kilometres, and shows the two that suit how large a pixel is on the ground there. 'far' names another layer that takes this one's place away from the eye, between 'farFrom' and 'farTo' metres, and is laid at one size, 'farSize' metres a repeat, whatever the distance (a wood's floor gives way to its canopy where the single trees the game draws thin out; a crown has a size, as grass and rock do not). 'gain', 'sat', 'warm' adjust the colours; 'ao' is how much of the material's own shade is kept in its colours (0.5); 'relief' scales its normal map. 'try' lists others to look at on a second sheet, without packing them.
_rule: Take scans made from the air, or of ground with nothing on it a person would know the size of: a twig or a leaf laid out a hundred times larger is a log or a tarpaulin.
_order: The game's shader knows the layers by their place in this list (0 meadow ... 19 beach): add at the end, and do not reorder.
